title: Enterprise SQ-linked I/O Floor with SLA Credits and Audit-compliant Metering
creator: Ava Sharma
description:
Summary: Propose and validate a billing experiment that ties per-direction input/output floors to enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ) acceptance and SLA commitment levels. The goal is to offer enterprise customers an audit-compliant meter and an optional I/O floor discount that activates only after a security questionnaire and SLA attachment are completed. This aligns procurement/legal acceptance with pricing protections for Redwood.

Background: Customers negotiating enterprise contracts often ask for billing predictability and audit trails. Current hosted API floors and streaming minimums are negotiated ad-hoc in sales cycles which slows procurement and exposes Redwood to billing leakage when contracts lack auditable acceptance. This ticket creates a standardized experiment to: 1) link an I/O floor feature to an SQ completion gate; 2) provide SLA-backed credits that partially offset the floor during the onboarding window; 3) emit audit events and meter snapshots that satisfy compliance teams.

Hypothesis: If enterprise customers can receive a conditional I/O floor discount only after completing the SQ and attaching an SLA, then the average time-to-contract will decrease (faster procurement), revenue leakage from undocumented discounts will be reduced, and overall TCV will increase while maintaining predictable gross margin.

Success metrics (primary):
- Median time from initial sales handoff to contract signature reduced by 20% within the pilot cohort.
- Revenue leakage from unapproved floor discounts reduced to <2% for participating accounts.
- No regression in per-token unit economics (weighted) beyond 3% of baseline.

Success metrics (secondary / telemetry):
- Adoption rate among eligible enterprise prospects >= 30% in pilot.
- Number of SQ audit events emitted per contract >= 3 (submission, approval, activation).
- Support ticket volume related to floor activation <= baseline + 10%.

Design / experiment outline: 
1) Product: Implement a flaggable billing modifier for hosted API that can: a) specify direction-specific floors (ingress/egress), b) be guarded by an "SQ-verified" account state, and c) schedule SLA-credit phases (e.g., onboarding grace weeks 0-4 = 50% credit).
2) Sales flow: Add a checkbox and automated SQ intake link in the enterprise quote template. Only after SQ state is set to VERIFIED in the account profile will the billing modifier auto-activate at next billing cycle.
3) Billing & Metering: Emit an immutable audit record (timestamped) when SQ verification and SLA attachment occur; store meter snapshots that show per-direction token counts and floor application windows.
4) Console UX: Enterprise Billing page will display activation status, audit events link, and projected charges with/without floor to aid procurement.
5) Legal/Compliance: Include templated contract language and an SQ attestation clause. Coordinate with security to map which SQ answers constitute verification.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (spec & security alignment, 2 weeks): finalize SQ verification rules and contract language.
- Phase 1 (internal pilot, 4 weeks): apply to two strategic customers with active sales cycles; manual overrides allowed by finance.
- Phase 2 (limited GA, 8 weeks): open to accounts in enterprise tier via self-serve in Console backed by checklist.
- Phase 3 (evaluate & iterate, 4 weeks): analyze metrics, tighten automation, and propose standard contract amendment for all enterprise deals.

Telemetry & experiments:
- Track cohort A (with SQ-linked floor) vs cohort B (normal negotiations) through sales CRM events + billing telemetry.
- A/B test two credit schedules (50% v 25% onboarding credit) to measure churn and procurement speed.
- Export dashboards: signed-contract lag, delta unit economics, audit-event counts.

Edge cases & risks:
- Risk: Customers may delay SQ completion to avoid minimums; mitigation: cap retroactive floor activation to post-signature periods and require explicit opt-in in the contract.
- Risk: Increased support load during activation window; mitigation: add an activation checklist and pre-populated FAQ in Console.
- Risk: Legal pushback on conditional discounts; mitigation: pre-clear language with Legal and create an "accepted-SQ" audit trail for disputes.

Required artifacts & links: 
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIC/PM-247891+SQ+I/O+Floor+PRD
- Billing design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/billing-design/pm-247891
- Acceptance criteria spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/pm-247891-acceptance
- Security mapping doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SQ/SQ+verification+matrix

Open questions for next sync: 
- Which specific SQ responses map to the "verified" state? (Security to confirm)
- Should floor activation be retroactive to signing date or only prospective? (Finance preference: prospective only)
- How many onboarding credit weeks minimize churn without losing margin? (Experiment to determine)
